top1.computed: the top 1%'s total income and disposable income are BEA's published top-1% shares; its owners' income is the top fifth's, split between 80-99% and the top 1% in proportion to the matching DFA holdings of the same income groups; its benefits and business transfers are the top fifth's per household; its taxes are BEA's top-1% personal income (households ranked by personal income) less its top-1% disposable income (households ranked by disposable income, the only ranking under which BEA publishes it), a mix of two rankings that likely understates the income-ranked top 1%'s taxes (the size per 0.1 pt of disposable-income share is in steps.rankingMix and taxesSensitivity); its pay is what is left of its personal income, with social-insurance contributions at the top fifth's ratio to pay
